skills_considered.reason: A complete local PMC XML was supplied; retrieval was limited to linked figures and supplements.
The operator fixed the sequential reading order.
BLOCK_BATCH_COMMIT requires dossier and candidate landing rather than canonical edits.
No intervention, dose or therapeutic window was tested.
The four canonical scientific files were intentionally untouched.

group_assessment.weighting: The Aqeilan laboratory is a high-volume primary WWOX group. Construct continuity is useful, but same-group observations are not external replication; small cohorts, pooled Wwox dosage groups and panel/reporting discrepancies retain full weight.

field_density.note: Pancreatic-cancer and TGF-beta intersections are broad; the direct BMP2 intersection is smaller and this study remains chiefly same-lab mechanistic evidence.

multihop.note: All 53 references were enumerated sequentially. Direct WWOX pathway and cancer references were linked without upgrading same-group continuity to independent replication.

corpus_crossquery.query: Where do pancreatic/PDAC, BMP2 and SMAD3 mechanisms already occur, and what boundary does PMID 36572673 add?
corpus_crossquery.note: Post-reading corpus audit found 13 file hits. This paper adds conditional pancreatic-acinar cooperation with KRAS, bounded by Wwox-alone negativity and untested pathway necessity.

retraction_check.result: Repository and indexed-record checks on 2026-08-10 found no retraction, expression of concern or correction.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: The local PMC JATS identifies PMCID PMC9792466 and contains the complete body, methods, figures, supplement links and 53-reference list; every used surface is fingerprinted.

entries.proposition: Pancreatic Wwox deletion alone produced no detected ADM/PanIN phenotype.
entries.snippet: However, no phenotypes were identified in the pancreata of WC mice, suggesting that Wwox deletion alone is insufficient for ADM and PanIN lesion formation

entries.proposition: The isolated-acinar experiment was designed to test a cell-autonomous component.
entries.snippet: To dissect cell-autonomous versus non-cell-autonomous neoplastic lesion formation, acinar cells were isolated from KC and KWC mice, then cells were cultured to assess their ability to transdifferentiate into ductal cells.

entries.proposition: Heterozygous and homozygous KWC mice were pooled throughout the study.
entries.snippet: Strikingly, no differences were observed between KWC mice harboring Wwoxf/+ and Wwoxf/f alleles. Therefore, we refer to these mice as identical throughout our study.

entries.proposition: The Figure 2 caption claims three mice per immunoblot group.
entries.snippet: Representative immunoblotting of WWOX of KWC (n = 3), KC (n = 3), and WT (n = 3) mice 1-month post-tamoxifen injection.
entries.anchor: Figure 2B caption, text half of replicate contradiction

entries.proposition: Figure 2B visibly contains two lanes per group, not three.
entries.snippet: Panel 2B prints two visible WWOX/loading-control lanes under each group label KWC, KC and WT, not three.
entries.anchor: Figure 2B, native-pixel inspection after effective-PPI preflight

entries.proposition: Tumours occurred in 16/64 KWC and 0/14 KC mice during follow-up.
entries.snippet: 16 out of 64 Wwoxf/+ or Wwoxf/f KWC mice formed tumors between the ages of 4–8 months while none of the KC mice (n = 14) formed tumors in this time range

entries.proposition: The tumour-incidence panel displays a binary 0/14 versus 16/64 comparison.
entries.snippet: Figure 5A prints no tumours among 14 KC mice and 16 tumours among 64 KWC mice, with three asterisks but no named binary-outcome test in the panel.
entries.anchor: Figure 5A, native-pixel inspection after effective-PPI preflight

entries.proposition: The WWOX knockout rescue is supraphysiological rather than restoration to WT level.
entries.snippet: Figure 6H prints rescue-expression values of 5.9 and 6.70 relative to WT and shows colony formation below the WT control.
